Events and Communication Between Components

Communication Between Components

The basic communication modes between components are as follows:

  • MAML data binding: used by a parent component to set data for a specified attribute of a child component. Only JSON-compatible data can be set. For details, see Component Templates and Styles.
  • Event: used by a child component to transfer data to its parent component. Any data can be transferred.
  • If the preceding methods cannot meet the requirements, the parent component can use the this.selectComponent method to obtain the instance object of the child component. In this way, the parent component can directly access any data and method of the component.

Listening for Events

The event system is one of the main methods for communication between components.

A custom component can trigger any event, and the page that references the component can listen for these events. For the basic concepts and usage of events, see events.

The method of listening for custom component events is the same as that of listening for basic component events.

Sample Code

<!-- When the custom component triggers the myevent event, the onMyEvent method is called. -->
<component-tag-name bindmyevent="onMyEvent" />
<!-- or -->
<component-tag-name bind:myevent="onMyEvent" />

Page({
  onMyEvent: function(e){
     e.detail // The detail object provided when the custom component triggers an event.
  }
})

Triggering Events

When a custom component triggers an event, you need to use triggerEvent to specify the event name, detail object, and event options.

Sample Code

<!-- In the custom component -->
<button bindtap="onTap">Clicking this button triggers the myevent event.</button>

Component({
  properties: {},
  methods: {
    onTap: function(){
       const myEventDetail = {} // detail object, which is provided for the event listening function.
       const myEventOption = {} // Options of the triggered event.
       this.triggerEvent('myevent', myEventDetail, myEventOption)
    }
  }
})

The options for triggering an event are as follows.

Option Type Mandatory or Not Default Value Description
bubbles Boolean No false Whether an event pops up.

For the concept of pop-up messages, see events.

Sample Code

// Page page.maml
<another-component bindcustomevent="pageEventListener1">
<my-component bindcustomevent="pageEventListener2"></my-component>
</another-component>

// Component my-component.maml
<view bindcustomevent="myEventListener">
<slot />
</view>


// Component my-component.js
Component({
  methods: {
    onTap: function(){
      this.triggerEvent('customevent', {}) // Triggers only pageEventListener2.
      this.triggerEvent('customevent', {}, { bubbles: true }) // Triggers pageEventListener2 and pageEventListener1 in sequence.
   }
  }
})

Obtaining a Component Instance

You can call this.selectComponent in the parent component to obtain the instance object of the child component.

A matching selector, for example, this.selectComponent(".my-component"), needs to be transferred during calling.

A selector, for example, a CSS selector, supports only the following syntax:

  • ID selector: #the-id
  • Class selector: .my-component

Sample Code

// Parent component
    Page({
      data: {},
      getChildComponent: function () {
        // The ID selector returns an object, and the class selector returns an array.
         const child = this.selectComponent('.my-component');
         console.log(child)
      }
    })

In the preceding example, the parent component obtains the child component instance object whose class is my-component, that is, this of the child component.
